did_you_know.text: Psalm 150 opens with the words “Praise the Lord” and calls people to praise God both in his sanctuary and in his mighty heavens.
The chapter presents two reasons to praise God: his mighty acts and his abundant greatness—that is, his great deeds and the greatness of his majesty, as described in the verse.
Verse 3 mentions three musical instruments: the ram’s horn, the harp, and the lyre. In this way, praise is expressed through both blowing and playing music.
Verse 4 adds the tambourine and dance, stringed instruments and the pipe, presenting a combination of percussion, string, and wind instruments.
The fifth verse repeats the word “with cymbals” twice and mentions two kinds of cymbals: loud-sounding cymbals and resounding cymbals.
The verses show that praise is not limited to a single sound: it includes the ram’s horn, stringed instruments, the tambourine, dance, wind instruments, and cymbals.
The chapter moves from praising God in his sanctuary and mighty heavens, through his mighty acts and abundant greatness, to a description of ways to praise him using voices and musical instruments.
The concluding verse expands the circle of those who praise with the words “Let everything that has breath” and ends once again with the call “Praise the Lord,” just as the chapter began.
